newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on Cargill, Japan demand.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on Cargill, Japan demand.

text.p: WCE canola futures ended up on Cargill and Japanese demand, traders said.

"We would have ended down with Chicago if Cargill didn't buy July," a trader said. "Cargill and Japanese exporters bought May at the close," a trader said. May WCE futures crush profit margin fell to -18.70 Wednesday from -15.75 Tuesday. May-July spread at $3, July-Nov at $62, May-Nov $59.80. Volume was 2,201 lots, or 44,020 tonnes, with 51 hedge lots.
Japan bought 2,000-3,000 tonnes of canola, sources said.
May canola ended up $3.40 per tonne at $427, July up $2.10 to $429.20. May flax fell $1.90to $356.10 on hedges.
May western barley lost $0.10 to $142, July rose $0.50 to $141 as Alberta Wheat Pool sold 600 May-July at $1 to another commercial, traders said. Volume was 1,450 lots.
May feed wheat was unchanged at $172, July lost $0.40 to $168.10 with AWP selling 200 May-July at $4 to $3.50. May-Dec spread at $4.50, July-Oct $1. Volume was 2,800 lots.
RBC-DS bought 10 May feed pea contracts from UGG unchanged at US$214.60. Oats did not trade.
(All values in Canadian dollars, except feed peas)
